key_insight: Composition-weighted elemental properties offer a low-cost route to screening unstable planar fault energies in multicomponent alloys through the shear-modulus–Burgers-vector product (μbₚ).
engineering_relevance: This approach could accelerate alloy screening for slip and twinning behavior without directly calculating every alloy’s fault energies.
method: Use embedded-atom method (EAM) potentials complemented by density functional theory (DFT).
Evaluate temperature and composition effects on unstable planar fault energies and their relationship with μbₚ.
Estimate alloy μbₚ from composition-weighted pure-element values.
evidence_signal: Alloy μbₚ correlates linearly with composition-weighted elemental μbₚ (R² = 0.95), while the UPFE–μbₚ correlation strengthens with chemical complexity in Co–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ni alloys.
watch_item: Account for systematic negative deviations in alloy μbₚ estimates; the UPFE relationship also deviates for intermetallics, non-close-packed elements, and some binary compositions.
paper_title: Predicting unstable planar fault energies in multicomponent alloys from pure elemental components
